purpose: Teach: まなざし/哀しい/長続き/パラパラ/ふい/呆然と/生れ/ただ今

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは家族を温かいまなざしで見ておられたぞ
lines.en: Gran — when your father was young, he used to watch us all with such warmth in his eyes.
lines.style: Slow, measured cadence. Voice settles into memory like sitting down after a long walk. Gentle weight on 'warmth.' Trailing off at the end as if looking at something far away.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、戦の話になると哀しい顔をされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, Grandpa — and when he'd talk about the war, his face would go so sad, wouldn't it?
lines.style: Soft, nodding quality. Speaking more to the memory than to him. Slight lift at the end of the question, inviting him to sit with her in the recollection. Warm, companionable.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんとの友情は長続きされたぞ
lines.en: Gran — the friendship he had with his own father when he was young, it lasted such a long time.
lines.style: Quiet reverence. Each word deliberate, like placing something precious on a shelf. Pause before 'lasted.' Voice doesn't rise or fall — just steady, faithful.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、雪がパラパラ降る日、お庭を眺められたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa — on those snowy days, you'd watch the garden together, wouldn't you?
lines.style: Soft wonder in the voice. 'Snowy days' opens with a kind of quiet delight. Slight breathiness. The question at the end is tender, not seeking information — just reaching for agreement.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがふいに帰宅されて驚いたぞ
lines.en: Gran — when your father came home suddenly one day, we were all so startled.
lines.style: Breath catches slightly on 'suddenly.' Voice picks up with a faint spark of the surprise itself, then settles back into reflection. Quieter at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、戦争のニュースに呆然と佇まれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa — you stood there stunned when the war news came on, didn't you?
lines.style: Voice becomes quieter, more serious. The question carries weight — acknowledging something difficult without flinching. Delivered with gentle certainty, not fragility.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お父さんが生れた村は、もう無くなったぞ
lines.en: Gran — the village where your father was born doesn't exist anymore.
lines.style: Final, matter-of-fact, but underneath it a deep sorrow. No apology in the tone. Simply stating what is. Long pause before speaking.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ただ今戻りましたと毎日仰ってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Grandpa — every single day he'd say, 'I'm home,' like he was still coming back to you.
lines.style: Voice fills with tenderness and ache. 'Every single day' is careful, loving. The phrase 'I'm home' is spoken almost as quotation — a ritual he honored. Close, intimate delivery.
